name: West Virginia

jury_list.statute: W. Va. Code 52-1-5a(e): juror qualification questionnaires are made available, on request, to counsel of record in the trial; after the trial they 'may only be released with the written permission of the judge who presided over the trial.' The county name list itself is open for inspection (52-1-5(g)), but it does not show disqualifications.

sources.cite: W. Va. Code 52-1-8 (court determines disqualification, including non-citizenship; clerk records it on the form and list)

voter_file.who_may_get: Any person may examine registration records at the county clerk's office (W. Va. Code 3-2-30(a)). Lists may be obtained for noncommercial purposes from the county clerk at one cent per name, or bought from the Secretary of State (3-2-30(c), (e)).
voter_file.permitted_uses: Noncommercial purposes. Not for commercial or charitable solicitation or advertising, and not sold or reproduced for resale (3-2-30(c), (f)).

private_challenge.who: The county clerk, the Secretary of State, any county registrar, a political party committee chair, or 'any voter who shall appear in person at the clerk's office' (W. Va. Code 3-2-28(a)).
private_challenge.form_or_statute: W. Va. Code 3-2-28: form prescribed by the Secretary of State giving the voter's name and address and the reason for the challenge, filed of record with the county clerk.
private_challenge.deadlines: No filing deadline stated. The clerk mails a certified notice; the voter has 30 days to appear with evidence of eligibility, or the registration is canceled (3-2-28(b)-(c)).
private_challenge.evidence_standard: Not stated. Returned mail or failure to appear is prima facie evidence of ineligibility (3-2-28(c)).

county_board.name: West Virginia county clerk directory (Secretary of State)
county_board.note: Challenges under W. Va. Code 3-2-28 are filed in person at the county clerk's office.

state_election_office.name: West Virginia Secretary of State - Elections

gates.basis: Juror questionnaires go only to counsel, or out with the trial judge's written permission (W. Va. Code 52-1-5a(e)). A voter may challenge in person at the county clerk's office (3-2-28). Strict gates: counts only.

notes: Caution: West Virginia cancels the registration if the voter does not appear within 30 days or the certified notice comes back (3-2-28(c)). A wrong challenge can remove an eligible voter quickly. This is a strong reason to keep guidance off without a lawful jury source.
Federal law: the NVRA 90-day rule on systematic removal programs still applies; 3-2-28 itself sets no pre-election cutoff.

dob_in_public_file is null: 3-2-30(a) says inspection files include all registration information except phone, email, SSN, and license numbers, and 3-2-18 says records hold birth dates, but no section says birth dates are on the sold lists.
official_pipeline is null: no jury-to-clerk non-citizen statute was found.
